business_problem: Worley needed to make decades of engineering knowledge usable in day-to-day project work, because staff were losing 20–30% of their time searching fragmented repositories and manually extracting information from CAD models, vendor datasheets, compliance reports, and other technical documents.
solution_summary: Worley built AI.Assist as a single virtual assistant for engineering knowledge and operational guidance, using NVIDIA NIM microservices as the acceleration layer. The platform unifies more than 100,000 documents and fifty years of expertise so engineers no longer have to jump among separate systems, logins, and file formats to find design or compliance information. Instead, employees query one assistant that can search, summarize, and contextualize knowledge across the company's engineering estate. By standardizing on NIM-based inference services rather than stitching together a series of bespoke tools, Worley created a scalable AI platform sized for tens of thousands of users and hundreds of concurrent sessions. The result is a governed knowledge layer that reduces manual search time, supports faster engineering decisions, and gives the company a reusable agentic AI foundation for EPC workflows.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA NIM microservices
solution_components.role: Provide the model-serving layer that powers Worley AI.Assist and its enterprise engineering search experience.

data_flow: Engineering documents and knowledge repositories are unified behind AI.Assist, queried through NIM-backed inference services, and returned to Worley engineers as summarized, contextual answers drawn from decades of project documentation.
business_outcome: Worley is positioned to cut common information-search tasks from more than 15 minutes to less than five, serve about 50,000 users across 100,000 documents, and maintain 99.99% uptime for a knowledge assistant that recovers a large share of the engineering time previously lost to manual search and analysis.
architecture_clues: Worley AI.Assist is sized for global use rather than a team-specific pilot.
The assistant is meant to replace multiple engineering repositories and interfaces with one knowledge surface.
NIM microservices act as the common serving layer for the enterprise assistant.
evidence_quotes: Worley set out to build a unified, intelligent AI platform from the ground up.
This new solution, Worley AI.Assist, brings together all of Worley’s engineering knowledge and best practices into a single, scalable virtual assistant—accelerated by NVIDIA’s full-stack AI platform.
Engineers can routinely lose 20–30% of their working hours navigating fragmented repositories
Worley AI.Assist is built to serve the entire global workforce, supporting approximately 50,000 users and providing real-time access to over 100,000 documents.
